div.head: RECORD SOCIETY.
div.p: THE RECORD SOCIETY.

On Tuesday the annual meeting of this society was held. Mr. J. P. Rylands proposed the re- appointment of the Rev. A. E. P. Gray and Mr. J. E. Worsley. of Warrington, as auditors. He said the volume of wills projected by Mr. Earwaker went hack to the will of Thomas de Macclesfield, dated 1302. It included also such names as Stanley, Davenport, Leg!' of Lyme, Jodrell, and many ethers of equal note in Lancashire and Cheshire, and the details were in many cases exceedingly interesting. Mr. Earwaker seconded the proposal, which was agreed.

div.head: CHRISTIAN POLICE ASSOCIATION.
div.p: CHRISTIAN POLICE ASSOCIATION.

A. meeting of the members of the Christian Police Association was held on Tuesday afternoon in the T.M.C.A., Friars Green. There was a capital atten- dance, end the meeting was presided over by Miss Bessie Dutton. After opening with singing and prayer, Mr. Renton sang "I love to tell the story," in a touching manner, the aulience joining heartily in the chorus. Mrs. Renton then gave an excellent address upon the text "Look unto Me and ye shall live." After the close of the discourse, Miss Wheatley rendered the solo "All I do for Jesus," in a pleasing manner. A very successful meeting was brought to a close by the pronouncing of the bene- diction.

div.head: SUNDAY SCHOOL PICNICS.
div.p: SUNDAY SCHOOL PICNICS.
LYMM CONGREGATIONAL CHURCH.

Harvest thanksgiving services were held on Sun- day at the above Church. Special music was rendered by the choir, and the church was tastefully decorated. The Rev. W. Williams. of Sale, preached at both services before large congregations.

div.head: LYMM PARISH CHURCH.
div.p: LYMM PARISH CHURCH.

The harvest festival services were continued on Sun- day, and were very well attended. It the morning the Rev. J. 'l'. Collins, curate l occupied the pulpit. A chil- dren's service was held in the afternoon. A full choral service was rendered in the evening, the anthem being taken from the words, "Fear not, 0 land" (Goss). The sermon was preached by the Rector, the Rev. G. W. Guest, M.A. The offertories were in aid of the choir fund.

div.head: THELWALL CHURCH.
div.p: THELWALL CHURCH.

The harvest services in connection with All Saints' Church commenced on Saturday nigt.a. On Sunday morning the service was very well attended. Special music was rendered by the choir, the anthem being taken from the words, "0 come, let us sing unto the Lord." The Rev. A. S. Pendleton, M.A., of the Diocese of Rangoon, preached on behalf of the Foreign Missions, from the words "Our Father." Collections were taken at each service.

div.head: HOLY TRINITY.
div.p: HOLY TRINITY.

The harvest festival was continued on Sunday, the church at night being thronged. In the morning the Rev. J. J. Langham, vicar of Padgate, occupied the pul- pit, and in the evening the Rev. R. Greendll, rector of Grappenhall, preached from the words : " He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man; that he may bring forth food out of the earth." Collections were made for the support of the day scheols the amount collected altogether being over £l4.

div.head: EMMANUEL CHURCH.
div.p: EMMANUEL CHURCH.

Harvest festivals were held at the Emmanuel Church, Bold-st., on Sunday afternoon. As is the custom at this place of worship, there were no decorations. In the afternoon the choir rendered a service of song, entitled "Harvest Home." Mr. Heron read the connective readings. In the morning the Rev. E. T. Reed preached a very effective sermon from the words, "So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her,which returned oitt of the country of Moab,and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest."

div.head: ST. PAULS' CHURCH.
div.p: ST. PAULS' CHURCH.

Harvest thanksgiving services were resumed at the above place of worship on Sunday, when the pulpit in the morning was occupied by the Rev. H. V. Pigot (vicar). In the afternoon a musical service was held, Dr. Garrett's harvest cantata being efficiently rendered by the choir. This, it may be meationed is the first performance of its kind in Warrington. The accompanist was Mr.Lythgoe, as usual. Tnere was a very large con- gregation in the evening when appropriate hymns were sung and the anthem " While the earth remaineth " rendered in a very creditable manner by the choir. The preacher was the Rev. Canon Dodd, M.A., vicar of Stretton, who is an old favourite at St. Paul's. He selected for his text the words "God lovettr a cheerful giver," from which an able discourse was delivered. At the close of the service a collection was made in aid of the cost ef the church expenses. The tasteful arrange- ment of the decorations was much admired.

div.head: PARISH CHURCH.
div.p: PARISH CHURCH.

The harvest thanksgiving services in connection with the above church v, ere recoinmenced on Sunday. After the morning prayer and choral celebration an excellent sermon was preached by the Rev. T. W. Cook, M.A., Vice-Principal of the Chester Training College,and former curate of the church, who took for his text St. John 4, 37, "One soweth and another reapeth. The musical portion of the service was rendered in excellent style by the choir. In the afternoon the children connected with the various Sunday schools in the parish attended the service, when the Rev. T. W. Cook again occupied the pulpit. The Sunday evening service was very wel attended. The anthem was taken from the words "fl will make mention of Thy kindnesses," (Sir A. Sullivan). Mr.Abdey rendered the tenor sololvvich great effect. Ihe pulpit was occupied by the Rev. J. Wakeford, M.A., vicar of St. Margaret's, Anfield, Liverpool. The preacher took for his text St. John ii. 8. He pointed out that they were prone to look at the material points of the harvest. They saw the farmer till the land and bring to bear upon its cultivation all his knowledge. Yet they must not forget that behind that was the power of Jesus Christ. The preacher concluded with an eloquent appeal to those present to prepare for the final harvest. The offertories were taken on behalf of the clergy fund and realized in the aggregate £42 ss. 10d.

div.head: CAIRO-ST. CHAPEL.
div.p: CAIRO-ST. CHAPEL.

The celebration of harvest thanksgiving services was held by the congregation of the above chapel on Sunday. There was no attempt at elaborate decoration, but the pulpit as usual, received the most attention,being freely decorated with oats, flowers, and fruit. The communion table was adorned with various flowers, principally white and coloured dahlias and sunflowers, and on the communion floor on one side were placed a group of vegetables and on the other three ingeniously made stacks—two of wheat and one of hay. These latter were presented by Mr. Forshaw. The ladies who had under- taken the work of decoration were Mrs.Drummoud,Miss Long, Mrs. J. R. Young, Mrs. F. W. Monks, and the Misses Monks. The sermons were preached both morn- ing and evening by the pastor,the Rev. W.H.Drummond, B.A.,and were most appropriate to the occasion. In the afternoon a special children's service was held in the chapel, the address being given by Mr. Thomas Birchall. J. P. The special anthem at the morning service was "0 Lord, how manifold are Thy works," and in the even- ing the well known hymn, "We plough the fields and scatter," was sung as an anthem to music composed by the organist, Mr. J. M. Muir, A.C.O. Both anthems were most effectively rendered. The congregations were large, and the services throughout were bright and hearty.

div.head: LEGH-STREET PRIMITIVE METHODISTS, WARRINGTON.
div.p: LEGH-STREET PRIMITIVE METHODISTS, WARRINGTON.

Harvest thanksgiving services were held at the Primi- tive Methodist Chapel, Legh-street, on Sunday. Mr. George fl. Wilson, a student from Manchester College, preached morning and evening to excellent congrega- tions. In the afternoon a service of song, "Sister Dora," was given by the choir, the connective readings being given by Mr. Cooper, and was much appreciated. Mr. Fred Atkinson efficiated at the organ. The chapel was pleasingly decorated for the occasion with flowers, corn, fruit and vegetables, contributed by the members of the congregation and friends. On Monday evening a fruit banquet, over which Mr. A. E. Watson presided, was held in the schoolroom when further gifts of confection- ery were received and distrinuted with the fruit at intervals during the concert, which was supported by friends from the Workingmen's Mission Chapel, Bank Quay. Mrs. Monks and Miss Ashley, Each contributed a song and afterwards a duet, for which they were heartily encored. Mr. Fred Astle sang. "Bonnie Mary of Argyle" and " Killa.rney " and was equally well received. Miss Edith Lawton, a very young child, gave two recitations, entitled, " Eva's Kiss," and " The Drunkard's Home," in a manner which caused many expressions of surprise at hey wonderful memory. Mr. Fred Atkinson caused amusement by his rendering of songs with banjo accompaniment, and Mr. Adcroft received well deserved encores for his clarionet solos. Mr. Fred Atkinson also accompanied singers and instru- mentalists on the piano.

div.head: BEWSEY-ROAD WESLEYAN CHAPEL.
div.p: BEWSEY-ROAD WESLEYAN CHAPEL.

The annual Harvest Festival in connection with the above chapel, was held on Sunday. The Rev. G. D. Mason occupied the pulpit in the morning, and the Rev. J. Kirtlan in the evening. It will be remembered that the festival should have been held a few weeks ago, but owing to the lateness of the season it was decided to postpone it. The chapel was well filled on both occas- ions, but especially in the evening, when every inch of sitting room was occupied. The'sacred edifice was beauti- fully decorated with flowers, plants, and cereals. Special pains had been taken with the rostrum, whicn was com- pletely hidden in foliage. In a conspicious place were fixed two small stacks, which were the only specimens of the harvest, the rest of the decorations being made up of gladioli, palms, dahlias, and a variety of other plants and flowers. The usual harvest hyms were sung, and the choir gave a very good rendering of the anthem, "0 God,who is like unto Thee ?" Mr. Baker taking the tenor solo and Miss Kent the soprano. Miss Kent gave a sweet rendition of "The Better Land." Mr. Wads- worth presided at the organ. The Rev. J. Kirtlan preached an appropriate and stirring sermon, taking as his text Leviticus xxv. 39-44. He said feasts had been kept by every nation on the earth, for they satisfied a want that was felt by human nature, and what was a real distinctive want of human nature must in some way be supplied. The Arcadians whose antiquity and civilization dated back beyond the days of the Egyptians and Babylonians, and who had left in stone evidences of their civilization and their literature—these ancient people had their feasts. The Romans had sa many feasts that at length they so far interfered with the ordinary duties of life that some of them had to be suppressed and regulated. The Greeks had a festival which was as popular as the harvest festival was to-day—tkat was a festival held in honour of the godless Ceres, who was the goddess of corn. Among the feasts of the Jews the most joyous was the feast of the Tabernacles, which re- presented our harvest festival. It tended to keep alive in the nation a deep sense of gratitude to God for the ordinary gifts of life. What an object lesson was the harvest ! In the first place, it was a standing miracle. Talk about the days of miracles having passed. Be could not understand bow a man could not believe in miracles. He could not understand how a man could believe in himself if he did not believe in miracles, because he himself was the greatest miracle of all. It required as much ability to develop the corn at the pre- sent day as it did to make the first grain. The harvest was an illustration of the recurring providence of God, and they were now assembled to thank him for His goodness. A coPection was made at each service on be- half of the circuit fund.

ST. JOHN'S CHURCH, EARLESTOWN. Special harvest thanksgiving; services in connec.. tion with St. John's Church, Earlestown,were concluded on Sunday. At the morning service the pulpit Wipe, occupied by the Rev. J. Andrews, of Haydock, and ia the evening by the Rev. E. W. Whittenbury-Kaye. In the afternoon a sacred musical recital was given by the organist (Mrs. Latimer) and the choir, the item sub- mitted being anthem " Blessed be the name of the Lord," organ solo" Andante in E minor," solo " His salvation is nigh," Mr. J. H. Lewis; prelude and fugue, Mrs. Latimer ; solo "I will sing of Thy mercies," Mrs. Kaye ; anthem" I will feed My flock ;" organ solo, variations on the" Harvest Hymn ;" duet, " 0 lovely Peace "Mrs. Kaye and Miss Matthews ; anthem, " Ye shall go out with joy." The total collections amounted to about £23.

div.head: ST. JAMES'S, HAYDOCK.
div.p: ST. JAMES'S, HAYDOCK.

Special thanksgiving services for the successall gathering of the harvest were held in St. James's Church on Sunday. The edifice had been very prettily decorated with flowers, fruit, and cereals, by the lady members of the choir,assisted by other members of the congregation. The sermon at the morning service was preached by'Lhe Rev. E. Whittenbury-Kaye of Earlestown, in the after- naion by the Rev. W. J. Melville, M.A. Rector of Ashton, the musical portion of the afternoon service being given by the choir of Holy Trinity Church, Downall-grcen. In the evening the pulpit was occupied by the Rev. C. J. Buckmaster, M.A., vicar of Hindley. rhere were very fair congregations at each service, and the collections which were in aid of the Day School fund, amounted to £l3 2s. 9-d.

div.head: ST. PETER'S CHURCH, NEWTON
div.p: ST. PETER'S CHURCH, NEWTON

Special thanksgiving services for the ingathering of the Harvest were held in St. Peter's Church Newton, commencing on Saturday evening, the first Anniversary cf the Re-consecration. The church was very prettily decorated, the font which was arranged with autumnal leaves and ferns from Lanarkshire, a cross of bracken, with a centre of sunflowers, circled with apples artis- tically arranged, the work of Mrs. Gillespie and Miss Barton. The pulpit was trimmed by Mrs. Matthews, Miss Mathews and Miss Thomas, and presented a lively appearance, bright flowers with ferns and moss, being prominent, and the tracing of the woodwork was picked out with oats and crab apples. The lectern had a group of plants, lent by Captain Royse, and was decorated by Mrs. Royse, two beautiful bunches of grapes sent by Mrs. John Jones of Mere House were prominent, with a basket of flowers and other fruit. Contributions of cereals, flowers and fruit were sent by Mr. R. Stone, and groups of foliage plants were kindly lent by Colonel McCorquodale. The altar and choir stalla also received attention and presented a seasonable appearance. The pulpit on Saturday evening, was occupied by the Rev. Canon Penrhyn, rector of Winwick. and the choir ren- dered the anthem "0 praise the Lord." On Sunday morning there was a lair congregation, the preacher being the Rev. Hon Canon Bridgeman M.A., rector of Wigan, the anthem sung by the choir being" Ye shall dwell in the land." At the evening service, the church was well filled, and a powerful discourse was delivered by the Rev. Lewis B. Radford, 8.A., assistant curate of Holy Trinity,Warrington, who took for his text " What doth this service mean." The anthem was" I will give thanks unto thee, 0 Lord." Mr. P. Fairctough presided. at the organ. The collections at all the services amounted to over £26, in aid of the debt on the enlargement of th• • church.

div.head: HAYDOCK
div.p: HAYDOCK

COLLIERY ACCIDENT.—On Thunday aftArnoon. a collier named Bradburn was adm,tted to the Cottage hospital, Elaydock. suffering from injuries received by a fall of roof, whilst following his employment at No. 2 pit, Parr.

NOTICE IS HEREBY ,GIVEN, that the next GENERAL QUARTER SESSIONS of the Peace for the COUNTY OF CHESTER will be holden at the COURT HOUSE, NETHER KNUTSFORD, in and for the said County, on MONDAY, the 15th day of October next, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when the Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all Appeals arising withinthe Hundreds of Bucklow, Macclesfield, and Northwich, forming the Knutsford District, and the trials of all prisoners com- mitted from such Hundreds, will take place at such Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury for the Knutsford District must be in attendance at the Court House, Knutsford, at the opening of the Court on MONDAY, the 15th day of October, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the, Forenoon. THE Court will be Adjourned to the Castle of Chester,. on THURSDAY, the 18th day of October next, at eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when another Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all Appeals arising within the Hundreds of Braxton, Eddisbury, Nantwich, and Wirral, forming the Chester District, and the trials of all prisoners committed from the last-mentioned Hundreds will take place at such Adjourned Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury for the Chester District must be in attendance at the Castle of Chester, at the opening of the Court on THURSDAY, the 18th day of October next, at eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. REGINALD POTTS, Clerk of the Peace for the County of Chester. Chester, 24th September, 1894.
